text:
maria: FYI posted a short RFC follow-up — trying to land a focused plan for consolidating our credentialing surface (api keys, service tokens, org vs project scoping). link: https://rfc/redwood/cred-surface

devin: skimmed it. +1 on shrinking the public surface. curious about the migration story for existing project keys though

maria: good call. thinking of a compatibility shim that accepts old project keys and emits a short-lived service token under the hood for new flows

sam: how do we map RBAC? currently roles are attached to API keys at project-level. if we canonicalize to service identities we need clear role-binding semantics

alex: proposal: introduce two primitive types: "identity-key" (long-lived, owner-level, only for minting) and "session-token" (short-lived, scoped). RBAC attaches to identities and session tokens inherit the intersection of requested scope + identity grants

lina: ping @maria — we need to ensure operator paths (cron jobs, background workers) can still use non-interactive creds without huge churn :thumbsup:

maria: agreed. operator path stays supported via identity-keys but we'll require rotation + HSM-backed storage for enterprise/private customers. default for hosted will encourage session-token use

devin: any perf concerns? token exchange per-request could add latency. maybe cache exchanged tokens per caller+route for N seconds

sam: caching sounds fine. also consider prefix/KV caching in runtime — we can tag cache entries with session-token id so revocation propagates

alex: edge case: third-party integrators that need cross-org access. do we allow org-scoped service identities, or brokered delegation?

maria: prefer brokered delegation using a signed delegation object. avoids global org keys. delegation object example in RFC: ```{\n  delegator: org-A,\n  delegatee: svc-abc,\n  scopes: ["embeddings:read","inference:call"],\n  expires: 1699999999,\n  signature: <sig>\n}```

lina: how about tooling for migration? can we provide a one-shot migration tool that scans project keys, emits identity-keys, and rotates clients with minimal downtime

devin: implement server-side fallback: if old key used, accept and return a Deprecation header plus minted session-token for callers. gives us time window to onboard clients

sam: ops question — telemetry for key usage (per-route, per-key) needs to be compatible across old and new surfaces. keep a canonical key-id that persists through migration

maria: yes — canonical_id will be our anchor. identity-key and legacy project-key will map to canonical_id during migration period. logs/metrics use canonical_id for billing/alerts

alex: one more: revocation semantics. short-lived session-tokens => instant revocation is tricky. we need token blacklist + realtime revocation events to runtime nodes

devin: runtime already consumes revocation stream (via pubsub). add token id to stream, runtime evicts caches immediately. small perf hit but ok

maria: next steps: (1) add compatibility shim + deprecation headers (2) implement canonical_id mapping in auth service (3) runtime revocation hook + cache tag (4) migration tooling + docs. I'll draft a short rollout checklist

infra-bot: RFC update: "credentialing-surface-primitives" merged to staging. CI: 12/14 checks passed, remaining: e2e-migration-suite

lina: cool — can we get a quick spike on the token-exchange latency impact? I'll volunteer to run perf tests

maria: thanks! Lina + Devin to pair on spike. I'll circulate the checklist and timeline. :rocket:

devin: noted, I'll schedule a 30min sync tomorrow

sam: :+1:

alex: thanks all — excited to simplify this surface and make migration low-friction
